items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: Bob Whiteman came back and I said

ctx.x: And I said, 'Well, you're not going to remove --,' Bob Whiteman came back and I said, 'You're not going to remove anybody. I mean --,' He said, 'Read the small print in the contract.' And it says down there that the theater has the right to remove anybody from the show that they think is not for the best interests of the show and so forth and so on, and to edit any material that might be being used and so forth, if it was detrimental. And I went to Lena, and I had a contract with her. I've still got the contract,…

at that time -- I don't know, John Hammond or Leonard Feather or somebody like that, they got her in Cafe Society or something, and I said, "I think -- don't worry about any contract you might have with me, because if I can't protect you I don't deserve to have you." And of course she went on. And she was getting -- you know, a lot of people were noticing her, and she certainly didn't belong being a band singer. She was too much.
